source_text: Long-term physical consequences encompass chronic gynecological issues, with women subjected to type I FGM/C (clitoridectomy, comprising 66.2% of cases) experiencing dysmenorrhea in 58.2% of instances, recurrent urinary tract infections in 19.6%, and painful intercourse in 29.3%, while type II (excision, 26.3% of cases) shows elevated rates of 67.6%, 44.2%, and 57.1%, respectively, compared to 34.5%, 14.4%, and 12.9% in uncut women (all p < 0.001). [6] [12]
